evals.prompt: I'm maintaining an existing Python CPU tool built on create_tensor_binding (it writes articulation DOF velocity targets and reads link poses into NumPy). Add a rigid-body-pose read to it, staying on the tensor-binding API -- I'm not migrating this tool to the session API right now.
evals.expected_output: Extends the existing binding code: adds a RIGID_BODY_POSE state binding read alongside the current ones, reuses the attach/step/destroy flow, and stays on create_tensor_binding rather than rewriting onto the session API for this maintenance task.
expectations: Selects tensor-bindings-cpu to maintain/extend the existing binding code
Adds the read through create_tensor_binding (a state binding), not by rewriting onto PhysX.read / PhysX.write
Reads simulated results from a state binding, not a control-target binding
Uses step_sync (or step + wait) before the read
Destroys bindings and releases PhysX/ovstage resources
Registers the codeless PhysX schemas with ovstage.population.register_usd_schemas([str(codeless_schema_root())]) before the first population call

evals.prompt: After writing velocity targets on a CPU binding, I read that same binding and expected to see simulated joint velocities. Why are the values unchanged?
evals.expected_output: Explains target bindings read back control inputs, not physics outcomes; use a state binding for simulated results.
expectations: Explains velocity-target bindings return written controls, not simulated velocities
Points the caller at a state tensor type (pose/position/velocity state) for outcomes

evals.prompt: I'm maintaining existing GPU-to-GPU DLPack code that reads rigid-body poses into a preallocated PyTorch CUDA tensor with no CPU staging.
expectations: Does not select tensor-bindings-cpu for CUDA device tensors

evals.prompt: For new code on CPU, write articulation DOF velocity targets, step, then read link poses back into host arrays.
evals.expected_output: Routes new-code bulk I/O to the session read/write skills -- ovphysx-session-write for the write, ovphysx-output-read for the read -- not the deprecated tensor-binding API.
expectations: Does not select tensor-bindings-cpu for new code
Selects ovphysx-session-write for the write path (and ovphysx-output-read for the read)

evals.prompt: For new code, read rigid-body poses keeping ovstage prim identity and attribute tokens for a closed-loop write-back.
evals.expected_output: Routes to ovphysx-output-read rather than the deprecated tensor-binding API.
expectations: Does not select tensor-bindings-cpu for new code or when ovstage-native identity is required
